🌐 CoinDCX has confirmed losing 15.99 million USDT through compromised wallet infrastructure after initially rejecting claims that nearly $16 million had been stolen from the Indian cryptocurrency exchange. The exchange said a failure in its automated deposit-sweeping service allowed cryptocurrency to accumulate at an address that customers continued using despite instructions to switch to newer wallets. ⚠️ The admission follows several days of disagreement between CoinDCX executives and blockchain investigators over suspicious transactions involving wallets linked to the exchange. On October 22, CoinDCX CEO Sumit Gupta rejected suggestions of another security breach, saying the flagged addresses belonged to infrastructure compromised in July 2025. He maintained that no funds had moved from current operational wallets into the addresses under scrutiny.

📊 However, the company’s latest statement confirms that deposits continued arriving at those addresses and that its own systems were responsible for transferring them to secure wallets when the automated service functioned correctly. Lately, I've been interviewing AI Engineer candidates with 1–2 years of experience.

One thing surprised me.
Almost everyone can talk about RAG.
Almost everyone has built AI agents.

Most have used LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI, Claude, or Gemini.
But when the conversation moves beyond frameworks...
...that's where many interviews start to slow down.

I ask simple questions like:
"Why do embeddings work?"
"Why does chunk size affect retrieval?"
"Why does an attention mechanism matter?"
"What actually happens before an LLM generates the first token?"

The room usually goes quiet.
It made me realize something.
We're getting really good at building AI applications.

But we're slowly skipping the fundamentals that make those applications reliable.
AI tools can write code.
They can generate APIs.
They can even scaffold an entire project.

But they can't replace your understanding.
If retrieval quality drops...
If latency suddenly doubles...
If hallucinations increase...
If your AI agent gets stuck in a loop...

The solution isn't another framework.
It's understanding what's happening underneath.
Frameworks will change.
Models will change.
The fundamentals won't.

That's why, before every interview, I'd rather revise concepts like:
→ Transformers
→ Attention Mechanism
→ Embeddings
→ Tokenization
→ Vector Search
→ HTTP & APIs
→ System Design
→ Memory
→ Databases
→ Evaluation
→ Python fundamentals
These are the concepts that help you explain why something works, not just how to build it.

If you're preparing for AI Engineer interviews, don't spend all your time learning the next framework.
Spend some time strengthening the foundation that every framework is built on.

Beneath America's cities, mountains, and military bases stretches a hidden network of bunkers, tunnels, and classified cities built for survival against nuclear war, natural disaster, and threats far stranger. Cheyenne Mountain in Colorado houses the NORAD complex, buried two thousand feet inside granite. Fifteen buildings rest on massive springs, sealed by twenty-three-ton blast doors built to withstand megaton blasts. Self-sufficient with vast water and diesel stores, the complex serves as a backup command center ready for activation. Hollowed from the mountain in the early 1950s, it contains three-story buildings on seismic springs, sealed by thirty-ton doors, with power stations, reservoirs, and capacity for thousands. And here’s one simple thing that’s important to understand. Almost everything in the global economy ultimately comes down to energy. More expensive oil means higher transportation costs, higher production costs, and more expensive goods and services. If oil stays above $110 for an extended period, it will give inflation another boost.

From there, a familiar chain reaction kicks in. Inflation rises, the Fed has a harder time cutting rates, borrowing costs stay high, and pressure on stocks and crypto intensifies. That’s exactly why the current rise in oil prices matters much more to the market than it might seem at first glance.

There’s another risk on the horizon: November 3, when the U.S. midterm elections take place. Reports are already emerging that another round of strikes on Iran could be under discussion specifically after the elections. That doesn’t mean the war will necessarily escalate. But after November 3, the political constraints on the White House could genuinely change, and the market is already starting to factor that in.

For us, the priority right now isn’t trying to call the bottom, but watching oil as one of the key risk indicators. As long as Brent stays above $110, any positive news for stocks or crypto could quickly be overshadowed by inflation concerns and high interest rates. On the other hand, a sustained decline in oil prices could be the first sign that pressure on the markets is starting to ease.

It’s called “close your eyes and immunize.” He says it’s becoming very common to vaccinate children when they go under anesthesia WITHOUT PARENT CONSENT often times because the parents are signing to do what’s best for the child under anesthesia, but doctors are now including vaccinations as necessary

Again, you take your child in for a surgery, sign the paper saying to do what’s best for your child, the hospitals are now using that consent to vaccinate your kids without your knowledge. Including with the COVID vaccine

“I'm a family doctor who practices in the suburbs and the city of Chicago. I wanted to offer some practical advice tonight to those of you who, like me, might be angry and very concerned about the news reports detailing the rise of what one hospital is calling, close your eyes, we'll immunize. This is a growing practice, perhaps pioneered at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, but something that's been around longer than the powers that be would like us to know,  where children are undergoing elective and emergency medical surgeries and being immunized while they're away from their parents in the operating room”

“Parents have often given consent unknowingly or under duress for these vaccinations to be performed. And one of the things that's clear from the reports is that informed consent, which should be one of the hallmarks of medical ethics and practice today, is rarely being provided to the extent that it should be”

“Flu shot seems to be the most popular thing to administer, but RSV, COVID, and some other things are now being administered without the parents knowing while their child is in the hospital. So imagine you take your child to the hospital because they have terrible belly pain. Turns out they have appendicitis and any of appendix taken out. You sign a form saying that the surgeon and the medical team can do whatever they think is necessary to help your child. You didn't know your child's getting a flu shot 15 minutes later before the first incision is made”

Okay this is CRIMINAL in my opinion so I did my own research and found out what states this is happening in,

Illinois at Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children’s Hospital of Chicago and its ambulatory surgery centers. Offers flu shots under anesthesia for eligible patients age 6 months and older during scheduled surgeries and procedures
